headline: Higher Ed's Enrollment Data Splits Down the Middle as Brookings and EdTech Digest Push Schools to 'Go Slow' on AI
thesis: Inside Higher Ed's same-week data shows record enrollment gains at some colleges and a shrinking humanities pipeline at others, while Brookings and EdTech Digest separately argue AI adoption in schools needs deliberate, human-centered pacing rather than a rush to deploy.
summary: Inside Higher Ed leads with three same-week, data-driven stories that together paint a fractured picture of the sector: institutions are reporting record enrollment turnarounds even as national data shows humanities bachelor's degrees at their lowest point since 1991, and a new ACE survey finds senior college leaders anxious about financial pressure and public skepticism. That uncertainty runs alongside a parallel AI story: EdTech Magazine reports K-12 districts are handing routine IT help-desk tickets to agentic AI while its higher-ed coverage ties AI adoption directly to enrollment pressure, and ISTE+ASCD announces a Google partnership to bring AI literacy training to six million educators. But a counter-narrative keeps surfacing: Brookings argues schools should go slow to go fast on AI, MIT's own AI report calls for rethinking grading and social learning, and EdTech Digest's guest column urges a more intentional, human-centered approach to classroom technology, citing new federal tech-use guidance for the school year. Equity questions run underneath both threads — Brookings finds screen-time bans disproportionately discipline Black students, THE Journal covers CoSN's push for purpose-based screen-time policy over blanket limits, and EdTech Magazine explores what brain-computer interfaces could mean for students with disabilities. On security, THE Journal's warning about unsanctioned shadow AI use echoes into EdTech Magazine's higher-ed coverage of balancing AI innovation with secure core systems. The fall conference calendar keeps filling in: 1EdTech's Learning Impact Europe convenes in Thessaloniki next week, EdTech Week and the StartEd CEO Summit head to Columbia University in October, and Ed-Fi's Alliance Summit follows in November.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · September 11, 2026 · Items were sourced and dated via web-search indexing rather than live page fetches this run (direct fetches to source sites were blocked by network egress restrictions); Education Technology Insights and Ed-Fi Alliance had no September-dated coverage surface in search, so their most relevant recent items are listed instead with a note.

themes.title: Same-Week Data Paints a Higher Ed Enrollment Paradox
themes.body: Inside Higher Ed reports institutions seeing record enrollment turnarounds for a second straight fall, even as national data shows humanities bachelor's degrees at their lowest point since 1991 and an ACE survey finds senior college leaders anxious about financial pressure and public skepticism.

themes.title: Agentic AI Becomes Everyday Infrastructure
themes.body: EdTech Magazine reports K-12 districts are deploying agentic AI to autonomously triage IT help-desk tickets, while ISTE+ASCD announces a partnership with Google to bring AI literacy training to six million educators as AI adoption ties directly into higher ed's enrollment pressures.

themes.title: A Counter-Narrative: Go Slow to Go Fast on AI
themes.body: Brookings argues schools should adopt AI deliberately rather than rush rollout, MIT's own AI report calls for rethinking grading and social learning amid eroded trust, and EdTech Digest's guest column urges a human-centered approach to classroom technology, citing new federal tech-use guidance.

themes.title: Screen-Time Rules and Accessibility Deadlines Test Equity Lines
themes.body: Brookings finds blanket phone and screen-time bans disproportionately increase discipline against Black students, THE Journal covers CoSN's push for purpose-based screen-time policy over blanket limits, and EdTech Magazine explores what brain-computer interfaces could mean for students with disabilities.

themes.title: Shadow AI and Weak Core Systems Keep IT Leaders on Edge
themes.body: THE Journal warns unsanctioned shadow AI use by students and staff is becoming K-12's biggest cybersecurity blind spot, while EdTech Magazine's higher-ed coverage examines the challenge of balancing AI innovation with secure core campus systems.

themes.title: Fall Conference Season Fills the Calendar From Thessaloniki to Columbia
themes.body: 1EdTech's Learning Impact Europe convenes in Thessaloniki September 15-17, EdTech Week and the StartEd CEO Summit head to Columbia University in October, Ed-Fi's Alliance Summit follows in November, and ISTE+ASCD's certification cohorts close enrollment September 15 and 17.
